To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the first component of the cytosol receptor for cortisol in rat liver was found to bind about 78% of the total bound hormone in normal rats and about 95% of the total in adrenalectomy rats, while the second receptor component binds about 20% of the total [3H]-cortisol in normal rats and only about 4.5 % of the total bound [3 H] cortisol in adrenalectomic rats.
the binding of [3H]cortisol to two distinct components in hepatic cytoplasmic receptor was altered by adrenalectomy.

(1) the first component of hepatic cytosolic receptor in normal adult male rats binds about 78% of the total bound [3 H ]cortisol to the receptor, whereas the second component binds only about 20%; and (2) after adrenalectomy, the first component binds 95% of the total [ 3 H ]corticosterone to the cytosol receptor, while the second component binds 4.5%.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the study of the molecular mechanisms of action of steroid hormones.
the mechanism of the interaction between the hormone and its receptors, as well as the role of the hormone in the regulation of nuclear RNA-synthesis in liver.
the mechanism of the effect of glucocorticoids on hepatic RNA synthesis.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
in liver cytosol the binding of [3H]cortisol is associated with two different components of receptor protein, which may have a different physiological significance.

the first receptor component in adrenalectomy is the one which is responsible for the biological action of the hormone, while the second receptor component may be involved in a different type of interaction with the hormone.
in normal liver, the first receptor component is the major one, while in adrenalectomy the second receptor component becomes the major one.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
there are two components of cytosolic receptor for cortisol, and the second receptor component is not detectable in liver of adrenalectomised rats.

the first cytosol receptor component is responsible for the binding of the majority of the bound [3H]-cortisol to receptor, and that the second receptor component may be a precursor of the first receptor.
the first component of the cytosol receptor is responsible for the biological effects of cortisol on RNA synthesis.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the first component of hepatic cytosolic glucocorticoid receptor in normal and hypophysectomized rats binds 78-90% and 95-100%, respectively, of the total bound hormone.
there is no single receptor for cortisol.
the second component of hepatic cytosolic receptor in normal rats may be responsible for the binding of a small portion of [3H]cortisol in liver cytosol.
